figmaBuildPlan.tokenProfileHint: Use default Techjockey typography with a trust-first light theme: Plus Jakarta Sans headings and Inter body. Since Zoho Desk is a customer support software, lean into calm authority with a light hero, strong logo-led trust strip, and clean white feature sections.

sections.variantHint: light-theme split hero with text left and product/trust emphasis on right; no form; no lead magnet; use CTA pair side-by-side
sections.notes: Use the full hero content: headline, subheadline, supportingLine, primaryCTA, secondaryCTA. Keep hero visually strong but not dark. Because no product screenshot is provided, use a centered-right brand/trust composition rather than an empty media area. Ensure the hero does not rely on a black or blank right side.

sections.variantHint: dominant logo-badge trust row with award badge and customer count stat; centered separators between items
sections.notes: This is the dominant trust signal per strategy. Place award badge first, then social proof text, then customer count. Use a light grey background block to separate from hero. Make logo-led trust the most prominent proof element on the page.

sections.frameName: Feature Section / Why Choose Zoho Desk
sections.variantHint: 4-feature layout, 2-column on desktop with readable cards; no nested grid inside grid
sections.notes: Use the four feature items from this section: Omnichannel Support, Ticket Management, AI Assistance (Zia), Workflow Automation. Avoid a dense grid inside a grid. Use clean cards with clear hierarchy and enough copy width for readability.

sections.variantHint: 4-feature layout, 2-column on desktop with readable cards; separate section block from previous features
sections.notes: Use the four AI feature items: AI-Powered Responses, Sentiment Analysis, Auto Tagging & Insights, Conversation Intelligence. Keep the structure consistent with the prior feature section but visually separated by section spacing and a section heading.

sections.variantHint: 5-feature layout adapted as 3-column on desktop with wrap, using compact cards or pill-cards for app categories
sections.notes: Use the STANDARD FEATURE label and the five integration items: CRM Integration, Collaboration Tools, Telephony, E-commerce Platforms, Automation Tools. Since there are 5 items, avoid a crowded single-row layout; use a readable multi-row card system that does not create nested grids.

sections.variantHint: partial content-aware feature section; continue only with supported items from the input
sections.notes: The input cuts off after 'Layouts, Customize ticket view'. Build only with the provided content that is actually present. Do not invent missing bullets. If content is incomplete in the source, show only the title/description block and any fully available feature rows.

figmaExecutionNotes: Keep the top strip fixed if implemented as a sticky utility bar in the system, but do not add unsupported form elements.
Do not add any form section because form is not supported by the input.
Do not add testimonials, news, pricing, or footer unless content is explicitly provided.
Use light theme throughout; hero should be light but still strong enough to anchor the page.
Maintain full-page scrollability from the hero so the entire landing page is visible and can be browsed continuously.
Feature sections must remain readable and must not use grid-inside-grid nesting.
Use only the sections supported by the provided contentMap; if a section is partially truncated, design only with the available text instead of inventing missing content.
Mobile should stack hero content, make CTA buttons full-width stacked, and convert feature layouts to a single-column readable flow.

heroStrategy.headline: Deliver Exceptional Customer Support with Zoho Desk
heroStrategy.subheadline: Streamline customer service, manage tickets efficiently, and deliver seamless support experiences across every channel.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unconventional asymmetric split: the media panel should sit on the left as a layered dashboard collage while the copy stack anchors the right, with the trust line and supporting benefits immediately below the CTAs. Keep the hero white-first with indigo CTA buttons, soft-shadow cards, and a faint mesh-gradient glow behind the product visual. Add a thin grid-overlay and small orbiting nodes in the hero for energy, but preserve the calm editorial B2B feel. This hero should communicate scale, AI efficiency, and omnichannel support without feeling busy; the visual language must stay polished, structured, and conversion-focused.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a split hero, then switch to a clean logo-proof band for immediate continuity and trust.
Use a tabs-with-preview product block after proof to create an interactive, visually different rhythm from the static hero.
Alternate subsequent product sections between split-panel-list and accordion-with-visual to avoid repeated card-grid density.
Introduce one darker emphasis band only for testimonials to create contrast before the final pricing and CTA-driven close.
Keep pricing compact and centered so the final section feels decisive rather than content-heavy.
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Desk Pricing, Features, and Support Platform Overview
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Zoho Desk, the customer support software for support teams and CX leaders. See how it handles tickets, automation, AI, integrations, pricing, and trusted customer proof.

sections.backgroundTreatment: light gradient with subtle dashboard-panel texture
sections.designNote: Make the hero content-first and continuity-led. Headline should answer what it is: Zoho Desk customer support software. Subheadline should clarify who it is for: support managers, CX leaders, and operations teams. Use a compact benefit line under the CTA with trust cues, but keep the primary CTA dominant and labeled only 'Get started'. Right side should show a polished product visual with ticket cards, omnichannel chips, and AI suggestion overlays.

Use 3-6 recognizable customer logos if available; since only a weak badge is provided, convert this into a tight proof row with the strongest available logo-style placeholders paired with the social proof message. Keep it compact and immediately after the hero to satisfy warm traffic continuity.

Begin with a tabs-with-preview block for the 4-feature core story: omnichannel support, ticket management, AI assistance, and workflow automation. This becomes the main feature explainer and should feel interactive and visually rich, not like a static grid. Subsequent product sections should alternate layout energy: one split-panel-list for Zia AI, then one accordion-with-visual for integrations and customization. Keep each section focused and avoid generic SaaS breadth.

Since whyTechjockey is absent, use this slot as a slim credibility-support block rather than a promotional detour. Keep it as a simple icon-list or counter strip if needed, with emphasis on implementation confidence, support, and secure cloud setup. This should be lighter than the product sections and not compete with proof.

Use a centered highlighted pricing card with the included plan features listed cleanly. The pricing block should feel decisive and low-friction, with one strong 'Get started' CTA in accent color at full opacity. Keep surrounding copy minimal so the value proposition is the focus.

Because there are 5 testimonials, use a carousel-static or compact slider on a dark-tinted band to create strong contrast before the final CTA. Keep quotes short, benefit-led, and tied to speed, automation, and self-service outcomes. This section should feel highly credible and emotionally reassuring.

Use the final conversion section as a centered floating card, not a split layout, to make the ending feel focused and action-oriented. Keep the CTA text as 'Get started' only. Reinforce the product with a short line about seeing Zoho Desk in action, and make the button full-width on mobile.

Do not use a moving marquee. If this slot is shown, render as a static flex-wrap strip only for recognizable logos or as a metrics fallback. Since logos are weak in the source, this can be omitted or converted into a final reassurance strip.

blueprint.designPersonality: Trusted enterprise support platform with a calm, efficient, and highly organized personality. The page should feel like a premium help desk system: clear hierarchy, strong proof, elegant spacing, and practical intelligence.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a polished SaaS dashboard illustration or UI screenshot-style composition in the hero, with floating support-channel chips, ticket cards, AI suggestion panels, and subtle line connectors to imply omnichannel orchestration. Keep the imagery light, structured, and product-led rather than decorative or abstract.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is moderately long and needs a strong but controlled size to stay elegant on a split hero without wrapping awkwardly.

colours.colourReason: Zoho Desk is a support/productivity tool, so it should use a clean white foundation with an indigo accent for clarity, modernity, and strong CTA visibility. This keeps the page aligned with the brand reference while staying distinct from orange-first Techjockey defaults.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-panel top hero with brand/logo anchoring, large headline, short supporting paragraph, and compact benefit list beneath. Uses strong left-aligned hierarchy and one primary conversion path rather than a split media layout.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero flows into a lead-capture/form block, then stacked content sections with repeating headline-description-feature clusters. Sections read as modular blocks with clear separation and consistent vertical spacing rather than dense multi-column comparison.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Utility-first content cards with simple borders or clean white surfaces; no evidence of glassmorphism, heavy shadows, or decorative card framing. Feature items are likely lightweight text cards or grid tiles with minimal icon treatment.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA-first conversion pattern centered around a form and a trial/request action. Secondary CTA may exist in the hero but the page prioritizes form submission over repeated button-driven navigation.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing module in the provided reference fragment.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not observable from the provided HTML fragment; likely a standard informational footer if present.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Mostly text-led page with minimal media usage in the provided fragment. Brand logo appears in the hero; no strong evidence of hero imagery, video, or media panels.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Repeated educational sections with headline, short explanation, and multi-item feature lists. Content is organized as benefit-driven modules, suitable for feature-grid or 2-column list patterns with progressive disclosure by section.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form placed immediately after the hero, using a card/container treatment and multiple hidden fields for tracking and routing. Form is visually separated from content and acts as the main conversion component.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, enterprise-style presentation with no explicit animated interaction patterns visible in the reference HTML.
designNotes: Prioritize clarity and trust over visual novelty.
Use strong typographic hierarchy and concise supporting copy.
Keep conversion controls early and persistent through form placement.
Favor modular sections that can scale from 3 to 5 features.
Maintain generous whitespace and clean alignment for an enterprise SaaS feel.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page should behave like a conversion-focused product landing page for a known SaaS product. Since the visitor trusts logos most, the layout should front-load brand credibility and social proof before deeper feature persuasion. Zoho Desk is solution-aware traffic, so the page should emphasize practical outcomes, AI support value, integrations, and pricing inclusions in a clean, efficient flow. A light, brand-like hero with a strong message and CTA is the best fit, while the rest of the page should stay airy, readable, and modular to support scanning and trust-building.
